body: Indian blow-ups repeatedly ran through promoter-level leverage rather than the listed company's own P&L: Zee/Essel (pledge 59% -> ~90%, promoter stake ~42% -> ~4%), ADAG (near-100% pledges; RCap, RCom, RHFL), Future Group (FRL promoter stake 47% -> 14% via invocations), Satyam (promoter stake ~25% -> ~8.6%, pledged), Kingfisher/UB (cross-guarantees), Cox & Kings. Mechanism: falling price -> margin call -> lenders invoke and dump shares -> further fall (reflexive), often triggered by a credit event elsewhere (IL&FS Sep 2018 froze MF/NBFC lending against shares). Signals: pledge % of promoter holding (disclosed quarterly under SAST; 'encumbrance' incl. non-disposal undertakings); rising pledge while price rises = borrowing against inflated value; listed company guarantees, letters of comfort, FDs or ICDs to group entities; MF/NBFC 'loan against shares' exposure to the group; promoter selling via 'gifts' or off-market transfers (PC Jeweller). Rules: pledge >25% of promoter holding or any rising trend = disqualifier for long-term holding; check all group listed companies, not just the one you own -- contagion is group-wide (Essel, ADAG, Future, IL&FS). SEBI disclosure since 2019 includes encumbrance reasons; track quarterly.

data.rule: pledge >25% or rising = disqualifier; check whole group

title: India: promoter pledges and group contagion
